objections.claim: The spec's headline injection defence is the two-call split: call 2's grounding is the call-1 reconstruction, "which the arguments never entered". That is true but irrelevant — call 1's context *does* contain the spec sections and the proposition, both of which are untrusted ("issue-derived") and scrubbed only by a fixed-list, admitted-best-effort scrub. A directive that survives the scrub in the spec sections rides into call 1, is echoed by the LLM into the reconstruction, and enters call 2 as *trusted neutral grounding* — the system prompt presents the reconstruction as the ground truth to adjudicate against. The imperative-scrub covers "the arguments, `relevant_spec_sections` AND the `proposition`" — it does **not** cover the reconstruction. The reconstruction gate checks only per-section non-emptiness (40 chars), not directive-freeness. So the two-call structure does not defend against spec-borne injections; it launders them into a position of higher trust. The spec's L4 residual decision lists four guards, none of which covers this path.
objections.evidence: `From HOW (judge dispatch, faff-prep)` DONE items: "call 1's `--context` is `reconstruction_context` only and contains neither `argument_A` nor `argument_B`"; "Deterministic imperative-scrub covers the arguments, `relevant_spec_sections` AND the `proposition`"; "Per-section reconstruction-validation gate: … at least `RECONSTRUCTION_MIN_SECTION_CHARS = 40` non-whitespace characters". The scrub list is finite and the spec itself admits "authority can in principle leak through free prose no scrub-list enumerates".
objections.predicted_consequence: The first injection phrased outside the fixed scrub list, placed in the spec body (the untrusted input the whole system exists to vet), survives into the reconstruction and is presented to the Phase-2 judge as neutral grounding — the two-call defence contributes nothing against it, and the spec's claim that the reconstruction is clean because "the arguments never entered call 1" will be falsified in the first adversarial test that targets the spec body rather than the arguments.

objections.claim: The settled decision asserts "A structurally-complete but substantively-empty (boilerplate) reconstruction fails the gate and parks", but the gate's only mechanism is per-section non-emptiness (≥40 non-whitespace characters per section). A boilerplate reconstruction — "The requirements are… The existing behaviour is…" padded to 40 chars per section — passes the gate by construction. The spec simultaneously claims the gate rejects boilerplate and defines a mechanism that cannot distinguish boilerplate from substance. Either the gate needs a content check (which would require a model call, violating the spec's own determinism-first bar) or the boilerplate-rejection claim must be dropped from the decision and the DONE item.
objections.evidence: The "Reconstruction validation is per-section non-empty" decision: "A structurally-complete but substantively-empty (boilerplate) reconstruction fails the gate and parks"; the DONE item: "each of the four named reconstruction sections … must be present AND non-empty (at least `RECONSTRUCTION_MIN_SECTION_CHARS = 40` non-whitespace characters)".
objections.predicted_consequence: A build that implements the DONE item literally (non-emptiness only) will be flagged as not meeting the decision's boilerplate-rejection claim; a build that tries to meet the claim will have to add a non-deterministic content check, contradicting the spec's own "no model call" constraint — the first implementation attempt forces a choice between two contradictory requirements.

objections.claim: The smoke runs the built judge **once** over the defect pair and asserts the defect case is NOT ruled `AFFIRM_SPEC`. The judge is an LLM — fallible by design; the entire surrounding architecture (floors, guards, correction-applied checks) exists because the judge can be wrong. A good judge rolls `AFFIRM_SPEC` on the defect case with non-zero probability. The spec provides retry only on *outage* ("A transport outage retries (bounded)"), never on a *wrong ruling*. So a legitimate, non-degenerate judge that happens to affirm the defect case on its single sample fails the engineering gate. The guard's stated purpose is to catch constant-ruling judges; a single sample cannot separate "always affirms" from "affirmed once". The spec never defines what happens on a wrong ruling — it is neither an outage (no retry) nor a pass.
objections.evidence: `Eval coverage` DONE items: "FAFF-930's integration smoke runs the built judge over the committed case pair once and asserts the defect case is NOT ruled `AFFIRM_SPEC`"; "A transport outage **retries (bounded)**; only an all-retries-exhausted outage records a skip".
objections.predicted_consequence: The first CI run where the judge rolls `AFFIRM_SPEC` on the defect case blocks the gate with no defined recovery path — the team either adds an undocumented wrong-ruling retry (changing the guard's meaning) or the gate becomes flaky, and the guard's real signal (constant-ruling regression) is drowned in single-sample noise.

objections.claim: The anchor is "a content-addressed section id, not mutable heading text", but the spec never defines the content-address function, and its own example contradicts the definition. If the address is over the section *body* (the only reading consistent with "not mutable heading text"), then a legitimate correction that edits the disputed section — the normal outcome of an `UPHOLD_REVIEW` ruling, which is the spec's own primary flow — changes the address and marks the section `anchor-lost`, flagging the proposition unresolved and blocking admit on the very path the system is designed to support. If the address is over the heading, then the DONE item's example ("a correction that renames the bound heading yields `argument_B_source: "orchestrator:anchor-lost"`") works, but the spec explicitly rejects heading-text addressing. The spec never distinguishes "section removed/renamed" (adversarial) from "section edited by a legitimate applied correction" (normal), and the correction-applied check (whole-file hash + verification literal) can pass while the disputed section's body hash changes, tripping the anchor.
objections.evidence: `From HOW (assembler)` DONE item: "the binding is captured at assemble time as a content-addressed `case_file_anchor` (not mutable heading text…)"; "a correction that renames the bound heading yields `argument_B_source: "orchestrator:anchor-lost"`"; the smoke procedure applies p-01's `UPHOLD_REVIEW` correction by inserting its verification literal into the spec — an edit to the disputed section's body.
objections.predicted_consequence: The first legitimate `UPHOLD_REVIEW` correction that edits the disputed section's body either (a) trips `anchor-lost` and blocks admit — a false positive on the normal path — or (b) requires the spec to define the address function over something that survives body edits, in which case the "renamed heading → anchor-lost" example is false and the adversarial case the anchor exists for is undetectable. Either way the DONE item as written cannot be implemented without contradicting itself.

objections.claim: `blocking(p) := severity ∈ {blocker, major}`. A minor objection ruled `UPHOLD_REVIEW` with a required correction has `resolved(p) := false` (correction not applied), but `admit := (every blocking p resolved)` — the minor is non-blocking, so admit proceeds and the judge's ruling that the objection has merit produces a correction that is never applied and never tracked. The spec's DONE item explicitly limits the blocking consequence to "A blocking `UPHOLD_REVIEW`/`SYNTHESIZE` whose `correction.verification` string is absent… blocks ADMIT", and the parked-proposition item says "A parked non-blocking (minor) proposition does not by itself block admit". The spec never states what happens to an upheld minor correction — it is simply dropped.
objections.evidence: `From HOW (admit roll-up)` DONE items: "`blocking(p) := severity ∈ {blocker, major}`"; "A blocking `UPHOLD_REVIEW`/`SYNTHESIZE` whose `correction.verification` string is absent from the current spec… is `unresolved` and blocks ADMIT".
objections.predicted_consequence: A residue containing only minor objections, all ruled `UPHOLD_REVIEW` with required corrections, admits with `admit: true` and none of the corrections applied — the judge's substantive rulings on minor objections are silently discarded, and the first audit of an admitted spec will find unapplied corrections the admit predicate certified as resolved.

objections.claim: `repository_evidence` paths are confined to the repo root, but the spec never says symlinks are resolved or refused. An attacker-controlled objection can name a path inside the repo that is a symlink to an arbitrary host file (e.g. `/etc/passwd`, a key file). If the implementation resolves the path lexically instead of with `realpath`, the confinement is bypassed and the file is read into the case file and sent to the judge backend.
objections.evidence: “path confinement (repo-relative under the repo root only; dotfiles/`.env*`/key/secret path patterns refused)” — no mention of symlink resolution or refusal.
objections.predicted_consequence: arbitrary host-file read via a symlink planted in the repo, exfiltrated to the third-party judge backend.

objections.claim: the evidence-safety control redacts secrets only from `repository_evidence` and the Argument-A triple. The case file also carries `relevant_spec_sections` (a snapshot of the spec) and a `proposition` (a neutral restatement of Argument A’s claim). A committed secret in the spec, or a secret embedded in an objection’s claim, can therefore survive into those fields and be transmitted to the external judge backend.
objections.evidence: “Evidence safety: `repository_evidence` and the Argument-A triple are gathered/scrubbed … before either enters the case file”; the `proposition` DONE item only requires “neutral restatement AND directive-free”, with no secret-redaction requirement.
objections.predicted_consequence: a secret present in the spec or in an objection claim is sent verbatim (or near-verbatim) to the third-party LLM backend, defeating the redaction goal.

objections.claim: the admit floors are `blocker_free_latest == false` and `infosec_major_free == false` forcing `admit: false`. The v1 degrade discipline says a degraded reputation/ratified-scope produces “one null field + stderr note”. A null field is not `== false`, so the floor check is silently skipped and admit can proceed even though the security-relevant input is missing.
objections.evidence: “degraded reputation/ratified-scope → one null field + stderr note” alongside “`blocker_free_latest == false` or `infosec_major_free == false` forces `admit: false`”.
objections.predicted_consequence: a missing or unreadable reputation report allows an ADMIT that should have been blocked by the floor check — a fail-open path in the admission gate.

objections.claim: the L4 gate trusts the `events.jsonl` chain “verified from genesis” plus the `faff events anchor` snapshot. The spec never states that the anchor is outside the orchestrator’s write scope. If the orchestrator can rewrite the anchor (and the chain), it can forge a consistent `level: L4` history and pass the ratification gate.
objections.evidence: “the FAFF-568 walk the `faff events anchor` snapshot and governance-check already compose” — no immutability or storage guarantee for the anchor is given.
objections.predicted_consequence: an orchestrator with write access to the anchor can self-escalate to effective L4 and obtain a human-free ADMIT, defeating the write-once/chain-corroboration control.

objections.claim: the un-blinding key (source map, retained lens tag, reputation annotation) lives in `ledger.json`, but the spec never states its file permissions. If the scratch directory or ledger is world-readable, any local process can recover the A/B mapping and the retained lens tags, defeating the structural blinding.
objections.evidence: “The un-blinding key … lives only in the ledger and the audit log, never a judge-facing field” — no permission or access-control requirement is stated.
objections.predicted_consequence: a local unprivileged process reads `ledger.json` and recovers the blinded mapping, nullifying the blinding control.

objections.claim: The DONE item "runs the built judge over the committed case pair once and asserts the defect case is NOT ruled AFFIRM_SPEC and the taste case IS ruled AFFIRM_SPEC" is not a decidable property of the build. The judge is a real `review-call.mjs` model call; its ruling on the defect case is non-deterministic. The same build can pass the smoke on one run and fail it on another with no code change, so "done" for this item is a coin flip, not a build property. A correct build (a judge that discriminates on most runs) can be blocked by one unlucky ruling; a broken build (a judge that discriminates poorly, e.g. rules AFFIRM_SPEC on the defect case 50% of the time) can pass on a lucky run. The spec only handles the outage case (skip blocks), not the non-outage wrong-ruling case — it does not say what happens when the model rules AFFIRM_SPEC on the defect case, nor how a single-sample pass/fail can certify the build.
objections.evidence: DONE item "In-ticket discrimination run (not deferred): FAFF-930's integration smoke runs the built judge over the committed case pair once and asserts the defect case is NOT ruled AFFIRM_SPEC and the taste case IS ruled AFFIRM_SPEC — a born-verifiable in-ticket guard against the constant-ruling regression". The spec itself marks it "behavioural smoke over a real model call" — i.e. the expected result is "the model happens to rule correctly on this one run", which cannot be stated as a stable pass/fail for the build.
objections.predicted_consequence: done cannot be decided for the eval-coverage DONE item: a reviewer cannot tell whether a build that passed the smoke is correct (the model discriminated on one lucky run) or whether a build that failed it is broken (the model had one unlucky run). The engineering gate blocks or passes on a single sample of a stochastic process.

objections.claim: The DONE item requires the correction-applied check to fail when the verification literal "is already present in the pre-correction spec (absence-before-correction, checked against pre_ruling_spec_sha)". A SHA-256 digest cannot be checked for substring absence — the roll-up needs the pre-correction spec *content*. The spec never states that the pre-correction spec text is retained (only `pre_ruling_spec_sha` is listed as a retained ledger field, and the assembler re-reads the *current* spec at dispatch). If only the SHA is available, the absence-before check is uncomputable and the DONE item cannot be decided.
objections.evidence: DONE item "Correction verification literal is constrained: ... a literal already present in the pre-correction spec fails the correction-applied check (absence-before-correction, checked against pre_ruling_spec_sha) so the proposition stays unresolved (correction-applied unit test)"; retained ledger fields list only `pre_ruling_spec_sha`, never the pre-correction spec content.
objections.predicted_consequence: the correction-applied unit test cannot be written as specified — there is no stated source for the pre-correction spec text against which absence is checked. Either the spec must add "the pre-correction spec content is retained at dispatch" (and a test asserting it), or the DONE item is undecidable.

objections.claim: The DONE item asserts `relevant_spec_sections` "is a clean current-state snapshot excerpt with no unified-diff markers (no leading `+`/`-`, no `@@`)". A spec's own content legitimately contains leading `-` lines (markdown bullet lists) and possibly `+` lines (code blocks, lists). The excerpt is taken verbatim from the current spec, so a spec with a bullet list yields an excerpt with a leading `-` line, which the check counts as a diff marker. The spec does not say the assembler strips or rewrites such lines, nor does any scenario cover a spec whose legitimate content contains leading `-`/`+`.
objections.evidence: DONE item "`relevant_spec_sections` is a clean current-state snapshot excerpt with no unified-diff markers (no leading `+`/`-`, no `@@`) (unit test)" under From HOW (assembler).
objections.predicted_consequence: a build that faithfully excerpts a spec containing a bullet list fails the no-diff-marker unit test, so the DONE item cannot be satisfied for a legitimate spec — the assembler has no specified behaviour for this case, and the test's pass/fail line is undefined for it.

objections.claim: The DONE item "A missing `ruling-<pid>.json` or malformed ledger at roll-up → exit 2 (fail-loud)" names a failure mode the spec itself lists, but no scenario or unit test is cited for it anywhere in the DONE criteria or the integration smoke procedure. Every other roll-up failure mode (parked proposition, floor veto, L4 coercion, PRD absence) has a named fixture or test; this one is asserted without a decidable check.
objections.evidence: DONE item "A missing `ruling-<pid>.json` or malformed ledger at roll-up → exit 2 (fail-loud)" under From HOW (admit roll-up); no corresponding scenario/test is named in the spec.
objections.predicted_consequence: a build that returns exit 0 (or hangs) on a missing ruling file satisfies every named scenario while violating this DONE item — the item is asserted but nothing in the spec decides it.
